items.title: Bike Lanes in the City
items.text: More cities are building protected bike lanes. Cycling costs far less than driving. (A), it keeps commuters fit without any extra time at the gym. Safety, however, is still a worry for many families. (B), accidents have dropped sharply on streets where the lanes are separated from traffic by low walls. Planners therefore hope that more residents will leave their cars at home.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: (A)는 장점을 덧붙이는 In addition, (B)는 안전 걱정과 대비되는 사실을 말하므로 Even so가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: The benefits of bike lanes and how they address safety worries
Why driving is better than cycling in big cities
The history of bicycle design in Europe
A plan to ban cars from every city center
qs.why: 자전거 도로의 장점과 안전 문제 해결을 다루고 있어요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what has helped reduce accidents?
o: Lanes separated from traffic by low walls
qs.why: 낮은 벽으로 차도와 분리된 도로에서 사고가 줄었다고 했어요.

qs.q: What does "however" in the fourth sentence signal?
o: An example of the benefits just mentioned
A result of the low cost of cycling
A contrast with the benefits just mentioned
The order in which events happened
qs.why: however는 앞의 장점과 대비되는 걱정(안전)을 이끌어요.

items.title: Change of Plan for Friday
items.text:
Subject: Change of plan for Friday

Hi everyone,

I'm sorry to say that Friday's photography club meeting cannot be held in Room 204. The room is being used for a make-up exam. (A), we will meet in the art room on the second floor at the same time. (B), please bring your cameras and the printed photos from last week. Mr. Han will bring extra memory cards, so nobody needs to buy their own.

See you then,
Jisoo

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 방을 쓸 수 없다는 원인 뒤에 결과(Therefore), 그리고 준비물을 덧붙이므로 In addition이에요.

qs.q: Why did Jisoo write this email?
o: To announce a change of meeting place
To cancel the club for the rest of the year
To ask students to join the club
To report the results of an exam
qs.why: 모임 장소가 바뀌었음을 알리는 이메일이에요.

qs.q: What should the members bring on Friday?
o: Extra memory cards for Mr. Han
Art supplies and a pencil case
qs.why: 카메라와 지난주에 인쇄한 사진을 가져오라고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does Jisoo mention Mr. Han's memory cards?
o: To warn members that the cards are very expensive
To ask members to return the cards on Friday
To explain that members do not have to buy their own
To say that the cameras will be checked
qs.why: so 뒤에 이유가 나와요: 여분의 카드가 있으니 살 필요가 없어요.

items.title: Sleep and Teenagers
items.text: Teenagers need about nine hours of sleep a night, yet most get far less. One reason is biology: during adolescence the body clock shifts, so teens feel sleepy later in the evening. (A), early school start times force many students to wake up while their brains still want to sleep. (B) the lack of sleep, students often struggle to concentrate and remember what they learned. Some schools have tried starting classes an hour later and reported better grades and fewer absences.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 두 번째 이유를 덧붙이는 In addition, 원인을 나타내는 명사구 앞에는 Because of가 와요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Teenagers sleep too little for both biological and social reasons
Teenagers should go to bed earlier than adults do
School start times have no effect on grades
Nine hours of sleep is too much for teenagers
qs.why: 생물학적 이유와 학교 시간표 때문에 청소년의 수면이 부족하다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: Why do teens feel sleepy later in the evening?
o: Their body clock shifts during adolescence
qs.why: 사춘기에 체내 시계가 바뀌기 때문이라고 했어요.

qs.q: In the last sentence, "absences" is closest in meaning to
o: times when students are not at school
qs.why: absences는 결석, 즉 학교에 없는 경우를 뜻해요.

qs.q: How is the last sentence related to the sentences before it?
o: It gives an example that disproves the problem
It describes a possible solution to the problem
It repeats the first sentence in other words
qs.why: 수면 부족 문제에 대한 해결 시도를 소개해요.

items.title: A Small Fee, a Big Change
items.text: When the town of Greenfield began charging ten cents for each plastic bag, shoppers were annoyed. (A), within a year the number of bags given out had fallen by almost 80 percent. Many people now carry cloth bags, (B) the beaches nearby are cleaner than before. Not everyone is satisfied, though. Small shop owners say they spend more time explaining the fee to customers. Still, most agree that the policy has done more good than harm.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 불만이 있었지만(However) 결과적으로 사용이 줄었고, 천 가방 사용의 결과로 해변이 깨끗해져 so가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Shop owners want to raise the price of plastic bags
Cloth bags are more expensive than plastic bags
A town has stopped all beach cleaning programs
A small fee greatly reduced plastic bag use, although some complaints remain
qs.why: 작은 요금이 비닐봉지 사용을 크게 줄였지만 불만도 남았다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: By how much did the number of bags fall in a year?
qs.why: 1년 안에 거의 80퍼센트 줄었다고 했어요.

qs.q: What do small shop owners complain about?
o: Customers refuse to buy cloth bags
Explaining the fee takes extra time
The beaches are too far away
qs.why: 요금을 설명하느라 시간이 더 든다고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about most shop owners?
o: They still support the policy overall
They plan to stop charging the fee
They think customers should pay more
They did not notice any change
qs.why: Still, most agree ... 에서 대체로 정책을 지지함을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Central Library Closure
items.text:
NOTICE: Central Library Renovation

The Central Library will close from March 3 to April 14 so that the reading rooms can be repaired and new computers installed. (A) the main building will be closed, the book-return box at the front gate will stay open every day. Members who wish to borrow books during this period can use the mobile library van, which will visit the community center on Tuesdays and Saturdays. (B), all due dates will be extended until April 21, and no late fees will be charged. We apologize for the inconvenience.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: Although는 양보(건물은 닫지만 반납함은 열림), In addition은 정보를 덧붙여요.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the notice?
o: To ask members for money to buy new computers
To announce a new library at the community center
To inform members of a closure and the services still available
To invite members to join a book club
qs.why: 휴관과 이용 가능한 서비스를 알리는 공지예요.

qs.q: When will the mobile library van visit the community center?
qs.why: 화요일과 토요일에 방문한다고 했어요.

qs.q: What will happen if a member returns a book on April 20?
o: No late fee will be charged
A late fee will be charged
The book will not be accepted
The member cannot borrow books again
qs.why: 반납 기한이 4월 21일까지 연장되고 연체료가 없어요.

items.title: My First Loaf
items.text: Last weekend I baked bread for the first time, and it was harder than I expected. (A), I mixed flour, water, yeast, and salt in a big bowl. Then I kneaded the dough for ten minutes until my arms ached. (B), I covered it with a cloth and waited for it to double in size. I got impatient and opened the oven too early, so the loaf came out flat and heavy. Still, it tasted wonderful with butter, and I plan to try again next Sunday.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 처음 단계는 First, 반죽을 치댄 다음 단계는 After that이 알맞아요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A simple recipe that anyone can follow perfectly
Why fresh bread is better than store-bought bread
The writer's first attempt at baking bread was hard but rewarding
How to choose the best oven for baking
qs.why: 첫 빵 굽기가 어려웠지만 보람 있었다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: Why did the loaf come out flat?
o: The writer opened the oven too early
qs.why: 성급하게 오븐을 일찍 열었기 때문이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "ached" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: ached는 아프다, 쑤시다라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How does the writer feel at the end?
qs.why: Still, ... 와 다음 일요일에 다시 해 보겠다는 말에서 희망적임을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Why Learn Another Language?
items.text: Learning a foreign language offers more than the ability to order food on holiday. It trains the brain to notice patterns and to switch between ideas quickly. (A), studies suggest that bilingual people often find it easier to focus on one task while ignoring distractions. A new language also opens doors to other cultures, since reading a novel in its original language lets you feel the humor and rhythm that translations often lose. (B) learning a language takes years of patience, the rewards are worth the effort.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 뇌 훈련의 구체적 사례는 For instance, 오래 걸리지만 보람 있다는 양보는 Although예요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Translations are better than original novels
Learning a language benefits both the mind and cultural understanding
Language learning is only useful when travelling
Adults learn languages faster than children
qs.why: 언어 학습이 두뇌와 문화 이해 모두에 도움이 된다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: According to studies, what are bilingual people often better at?
o: Focusing on one task despite distractions
qs.why: 방해 요소를 무시하고 한 가지에 집중하는 것이라고 했어요.

qs.q: What would the writer most likely agree with?
o: Learning a language is easy for adults
Only young people should study languages
Language learning is worth the long effort
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 노력할 가치가 있다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "lose" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 번역에서 유머와 리듬을 잃는다는 뜻이므로 fail to keep이에요.

items.title: The Clever Octopus
items.text: The octopus has no bones, no shell, and only a short life, yet it is one of the cleverest animals in the sea. In laboratory tests, octopuses have opened jars to reach food inside. (A), some have escaped from sealed tanks at night and returned before morning. Scientists were once unsure how an animal with such a short life could learn so much. (B), they now think that its large nervous system, which extends into its eight arms, gives the octopus an unusual way of thinking.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: (A)는 놀라운 행동을 덧붙이는 Moreover, (B)는 예전의 의문과 대비되는 현재의 생각이라 However예요.

qs.q: What have some octopuses done at night?
o: Escaped from sealed tanks and come back
qs.why: 밤에 밀폐된 수조에서 탈출했다가 돌아왔다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why were scientists once unsure about the octopus?
o: It refuses to take part in tests
It lives too far from laboratories
Its short life seemed too brief for so much learning
qs.why: 짧은 수명으로 많은 것을 배우는 것이 의문이었어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "extends" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: extends into는 ~까지 뻗어 있다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Hanbok in Everyday Life
items.text: For many years, the hanbok was worn mainly on holidays and at weddings. (A), today a growing number of young Koreans wear modern versions in everyday life. Designers have shortened the skirts and used lighter fabrics, so the clothes are easier to move in. Tourists have joined the trend, too. (B), visitors to old palaces in Seoul often rent hanbok to take photographs. Some critics argue that these changes make the clothes less traditional. Supporters answer that a tradition stays alive only when people keep using it.

qs.q: Which word best fills (A)?
qs.why: 과거(명절에만 입음)와 현재(일상에서 입음)가 대조되므로 However예요.

qs.q: Which expression best fills (B)?
qs.why: 관광객이 한복을 빌려 입는 것은 유행의 구체적인 예이므로 For example이에요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Tourists should not be allowed to wear the hanbok
Traditional clothes are no longer made in Korea
Designers prefer heavy fabrics for the hanbok
The hanbok is changing and becoming part of daily life
qs.why: 한복이 현대화되어 일상에 들어오고 있다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What do critics worry about?
o: The hanbok has become too expensive
Modern changes may make the clothes less traditional
qs.why: 변화가 전통성을 떨어뜨린다고 비판한다고 했어요.

qs.q: How do supporters answer the critics?
o: Old palaces should close to visitors
A tradition survives only if it is still used
Only holidays can keep a tradition alive
qs.why: 전통은 사람들이 계속 사용해야 살아남는다고 답해요.

items.title: Phones in the Classroom
items.text: Should students be allowed to use smartphones in class? (A), supporters say that phones are powerful learning tools: students can look up unfamiliar words, record a teacher's explanation, or share notes with classmates. (B), opponents point out that a single notification can pull a student's attention away from the lesson for several minutes. Neither side is entirely wrong. (C), a growing number of schools take a middle path, allowing phones only for specific activities chosen by the teacher.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
o: (A) On the one hand / (B) On the other hand
(A) On the other hand / (B) On the one hand
qs.why: 두 입장을 비교할 때는 On the one hand ... On the other hand 순서로 써요.

qs.q: Which word best fills (C)?
qs.why: 양쪽 모두 일리가 있다는 데서 절충안이 나오므로 결과를 나타내는 Therefore예요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A ban on phones in every school in the world
How teachers can record their lessons on phones
Arguments for and against phones in class, and a compromise
Why notifications are useful for learning
qs.why: 찬반 양측 주장과 절충안을 소개하는 글이에요.

qs.q: According to opponents, what can one notification do?
o: Pull a student's attention away for several minutes
Remind teachers to start the lesson
Tell students when the class ends
qs.why: 알림 하나가 몇 분 동안 집중을 흐트러뜨린다고 했어요.

qs.q: What does the writer think of the two sides?
o: Each side has some good points
qs.why: Neither side is entirely wrong 에서 양쪽 모두 일리가 있다고 봐요.

items.title: Teamwork in the Hive
items.text: A honeybee colony depends on teamwork. Worker bees leave the hive to collect nectar, (A) others stay inside to care for the young. When a worker finds a good patch of flowers, it returns and performs a "waggle dance" that shows the direction and distance. (B), the other workers can fly straight to the food without searching. This system is so efficient that a hive can gather huge amounts of nectar in a single season.

qs.q: Which word best fills (A)?
qs.why: 일부는 꿀을 모으고 다른 일부는 안에 머무는 대조이므로 while이에요.

qs.q: Which expression best fills (B)?
qs.why: 춤이 방향과 거리를 알려 주므로 결과적으로 곧장 날아갈 수 있어요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why honeybees build hives in trees
How honeybees work together to find and collect food
How to protect a hive from storms
Which flowers make the sweetest nectar
qs.why: 꿀벌이 협력하여 먹이를 찾고 모으는 방법을 설명해요.

qs.q: What does the waggle dance show?
o: The direction and distance of the flowers
The number of bees in the hive
The best time to leave the hive
qs.why: 춤은 꽃밭의 방향과 거리를 알려 줘요.

qs.q: In the passage, "efficient" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: efficient는 효율적인, 낭비 없이 잘 작동하는이라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Recycling at Our School
items.text: Our school's new recycling program is already making a difference. Since September, students have separated paper, cans, and plastic bottles into three colored bins in every classroom. (A), the amount of general waste has dropped by a third. The student council has also started a competition between classes, and the class that recycles the most each month wins a pizza party. Not all students take part, however. Some still throw everything into the nearest bin, (B) the council plans to put up reminder posters.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 분리배출의 결과로 일반 쓰레기가 줄었고(As a result), 일부가 지키지 않아서 포스터를 붙이려는 것이니 so예요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to open a pizza restaurant at school
A school recycling program and its results so far
A plan to close the student council
qs.why: 학교 재활용 프로그램과 지금까지의 성과를 다뤄요.

qs.q: How are the bins organized?
o: Paper, cans, and plastic bottles go in three colored bins
Each student has one personal bin
There is one bin for the whole school
qs.why: 종이, 캔, 플라스틱을 세 가지 색 통에 분리한다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why did the student council start the competition?
o: To lower the price of pizza
To punish classes that recycle less
To encourage classes to recycle more
qs.why: 경쟁으로 더 많이 재활용하게 하려는 의도예요.

qs.q: What does the council plan to do about students who do not recycle?
o: Ask teachers to sort the waste
qs.why: 일부 학생들을 위해 안내 포스터를 붙일 계획이에요.

items.title: A Late Delivery
items.text:
Dear Customer Service,

I ordered a desk lamp from your website on May 2 and was told it would arrive within five days. (A), it is now May 16, and I have received neither the lamp nor an explanation. I have written to you twice before. (B), I have checked the tracking page every day, and it still says "preparing for shipment." I would like to know where my order is. If it cannot be delivered by Friday, I would prefer a full refund.

Sincerely,
Daniel Park

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 약속과 달리 늦은 상황은 However, 이미 한 노력을 덧붙이는 것은 In addition이에요.

qs.q: Why did Daniel write this email?
o: To complain about a late order and ask for action
To cancel a refund he already received
To ask for a different kind of lamp
To thank the company for fast delivery
qs.why: 늦은 주문에 대해 항의하고 조치를 요구하는 글이에요.

qs.q: What does the tracking page say?
qs.why: 추적 페이지에 아직 'preparing for shipment'라고 나와 있어요.

qs.q: What will Daniel want if the lamp cannot arrive by Friday?
o: A discount on his next order
qs.why: 금요일까지 배송이 안 되면 전액 환불을 원한다고 했어요.

qs.q: How would you describe Daniel's attitude?
qs.why: 불만이 있지만 정중한 어조예요.

items.title: Hiking in the Rain
items.text: We arrived in Jeju on Saturday morning, and the forecast said rain all weekend. (A) the weather, we decided to follow our plan and hike Hallasan. The trail was muddy, and the top was hidden in clouds. (B), the forests along the way looked magical in the mist, and we met very few other hikers. By the afternoon our shoes were soaked, but we were laughing. The next day the sun finally came out, so we spent it on the beach.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 날씨에도 불구하고(Despite), 힘든 길에도 불구하고(Even so) 숲이 아름다웠다는 흐름이에요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: The best time of year to visit Jeju
How to prepare for a long mountain climb
Bad weather did not spoil the writers' hike
qs.why: 비가 와도 즐거웠던 하이킹 경험을 이야기해요.

qs.q: Where did the writers spend the second day?
qs.why: 다음 날에는 해변에서 시간을 보냈다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why were the writers laughing in the afternoon?
o: They had reached the top and seen the view
They were enjoying the trip even though they were wet
They had met many other hikers
They had found a dry place to rest
qs.why: 신발이 젖었지만 웃고 있었다는 것은 여행을 즐기고 있었다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "hidden" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: hidden은 보이지 않는, 가려진이라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Why Coral Turns White
items.text: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet about a quarter of all sea creatures depend on them. When the water becomes too warm, corals push out the tiny algae that live inside them and give them color. (A), the corals turn white, and this process is called bleaching. Bleached corals are not dead, but they are weak. (B) the water cools quickly, they can recover; otherwise, they slowly starve. Because reefs shelter so many fish, the loss of corals can also reduce the fish that people catch for food.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: algae가 빠져나간 결과로 하얗게 되고(As a result), 물이 빨리 식는다는 조건이므로 If예요.

qs.q: What percent of the ocean floor do coral reefs cover?
qs.why: 산호초는 해저의 1퍼센트 미만을 차지해요. 4분의 1은 산호초에 의존하는 해양 생물의 비율이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "otherwise" means
o: if the corals have bright colors
if the water does not cool quickly
qs.why: otherwise는 '그렇지 않으면', 즉 물이 빨리 식지 않으면이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does the last sentence suggest?
o: Coral loss may affect people as well as sea life
People should stop eating fish completely
Reefs will soon recover without help
Bleaching only happens in cold water
qs.why: 산호가 사라지면 사람들이 잡는 물고기도 줄 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How fish choose a place to live
Which sea animals are the largest
How algae are grown in laboratories
Why corals bleach and what it may lead to
qs.why: 산호 백화의 원인과 영향을 설명하는 글이에요.

items.title: What Volunteers Gain
items.text: Many people think that volunteering means giving up free time for nothing in return. In fact, it often gives the volunteer as much as it gives others. (A), students who help at animal shelters often say they become more patient and confident. (B), working with a team teaches them how to listen and share responsibility. Of course, volunteering must be balanced with schoolwork. Even so, two hours a month can be meaningful.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 구체적인 예(For example)와 또 다른 이점의 추가(In addition)로 이어져요.

qs.q: What does "In fact" in the second sentence do?
o: It gives an example of the common belief
It introduces a surprising point against a common belief
It shows the order of two events
It adds another reason for the common belief
qs.why: In fact는 앞의 통념과 반대되는 사실을 강조해 소개해요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Volunteering benefits the helper as well as other people
Students should quit their studies to volunteer
Animal shelters need more money than teams
Teamwork is difficult for most teenagers
qs.why: 봉사가 도움을 받는 사람뿐 아니라 하는 사람에게도 이롭다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What do students who help at animal shelters often say?
o: They no longer need any free time
They become more patient and confident
qs.why: 더 인내심 있고 자신감 있게 된다고 말해요.

qs.q: What does the writer suggest in the last two sentences?
o: Volunteering is only for people with free time
Two hours is too short to be useful
A small amount of time can still make a difference
qs.why: 한 달에 두 시간이라도 의미가 있다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Gardens in the Sky and on the Ground
items.text: In many crowded cities, empty rooftops are being turned into vegetable gardens. A rooftop garden needs little space, and it produces fresh food close to the people who eat it. (A), it keeps the building cooler in summer because the plants absorb heat. Community gardens at ground level offer a different kind of benefit. (B) rooftop gardens, which are often managed by a few residents, community gardens bring neighbors of all ages together to share tools, seeds, and stories.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 추가되는 장점은 In addition, 옥상 정원과 달리 공동체를 모으는 것은 Unlike예요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Different kinds of city gardens and their benefits
How to grow tomatoes on a rooftop
Why gardens are banned in crowded cities
qs.why: 도시 정원의 종류와 장점을 소개하는 글이에요.

qs.q: Why does a rooftop garden keep a building cooler?
o: The food is kept in the shade
qs.why: 식물이 열을 흡수하기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What makes community gardens different?
o: They are managed by only a few residents
They are built on the top of buildings
They bring neighbors of all ages together
They sell vegetables at high prices
qs.why: 공동체 정원은 모든 연령의 이웃을 모아 준다는 점이 달라요.

items.title: The Cost of Cheap Clothes
items.text: Fast fashion companies release new clothes almost every week, and the prices are low enough that shoppers can buy several items at a time. (A) consumers enjoy the variety, the system has serious costs. Factories use huge amounts of water, and cheap clothes are often thrown away after being worn only a few times. (B), millions of tons of textile waste end up in landfills each year. Some young people are responding by buying second-hand clothes or repairing what they already own.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 소비자는 좋아하지만(Although) 비용이 크고, 옷을 쉽게 버린 결과(As a result) 쓰레기가 쌓여요.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward fast fashion?
o: Fully supportive of its low prices
Worried only about the quality of clothes
qs.why: 환경 비용을 문제 삼는 비판적인 태도예요.

qs.q: In the passage, "landfills" are
qs.why: landfill은 쓰레기 매립지예요.

qs.q: What are some young people doing in response?
o: Throwing away clothes after a few days
Buying second-hand clothes or repairing their own
qs.why: 중고 옷을 사거나 가진 옷을 수선하고 있어요.

items.title: School Festival: Volunteers Wanted
items.text:
School Festival: Volunteers Wanted

The annual school festival will take place on October 24. We need volunteers to help in three areas: setting up the stage, selling snacks, and guiding visitors. Students who choose the stage team must be able to arrive at 7:30 a.m. (A), those on the snack team can come at 9:00. All volunteers will receive a free T-shirt and lunch. (B) you are interested, please sign up at the student council room by October 10. Spaces are limited, so early applicants will be given priority.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 도착 시간이 대비되므로 In contrast, 관심이 있다면 조건 If예요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of this notice?
o: To ask students to help at the festival
To announce the winners of a contest
To cancel the festival on October 24
To sell tickets for the festival
qs.why: 축제를 도울 자원봉사자를 모집하는 공지예요.

qs.q: What will all volunteers receive?
o: A certificate and a gift card
A bag and a bottle of water
qs.why: 모든 자원봉사자는 티셔츠와 점심을 받아요.

qs.q: Who is more likely to get a place?
o: Students who choose the snack team
qs.why: 자리가 한정되어 일찍 신청한 학생이 우선이에요.

items.title: From Bitter Drink to Sweet Bar
items.text: Chocolate began as a bitter drink. About 3,000 years ago, people in Central America made it by grinding cacao beans and mixing them with water and spices. (A), it was so valuable that the beans were sometimes used as money. When Europeans brought cacao home in the 1500s, they added sugar to make it sweeter. (B), it was still a luxury that only the rich could afford. It was not until the 1800s that machines made chocolate cheap enough, and solid enough, to eat as a bar.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 가치가 높았다는 사실을 강조하는 In fact, 달게 만든 뒤에도 여전히 비쌌다는 Even then이에요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How chocolate changed from a bitter drink to a common treat
Why cacao beans were used as money
How to make a chocolate bar at home
qs.why: 초콜릿이 쓴 음료에서 흔한 간식으로 바뀐 과정을 다뤄요.

qs.q: What did Europeans do to cacao in the 1500s?
o: They sold it as a medicine
They mixed it with spices only
qs.why: 유럽인들은 설탕을 넣어 더 달게 만들었어요.

qs.q: Which happened last?
o: Machines made chocolate cheap enough to eat as a bar
People ground cacao with water and spices
qs.why: 시간 순서상 1800년대 기계 생산이 가장 나중이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "luxury" is closest in meaning to
o: something expensive that is not necessary
qs.why: luxury는 사치품을 뜻해요.

items.title: Music While You Study
items.text: Many students say they study better with music playing. Research, however, suggests a more complicated picture. In one experiment, students read a science text either in silence or with songs that had lyrics. Those in silence remembered about 15 percent more. (A), instrumental music without words seemed to cause far less harm. The researchers explain that lyrics compete with reading for the same part of the brain. (B), if you need background sound, choose music without words.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 가사 있는 음악과 대비되는 연주곡은 In contrast, 연구 결과에 따른 조언은 Therefore예요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Silence is always the best way to relax
Instrumental music is more expensive than songs
Students should never listen to music
Songs with lyrics can make studying less effective
qs.why: 가사가 있는 음악이 공부를 방해할 수 있다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: How much more did students in silence remember?
qs.why: 침묵 속에서 읽은 학생들이 약 15퍼센트 더 기억했어요.

qs.q: Why do lyrics harm reading, according to the researchers?
o: They make the music too loud
They compete with reading for the same part of the brain
They are usually in a foreign language
They are hard to hear while reading
qs.why: 가사와 읽기가 뇌의 같은 부분을 두고 경쟁하기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about students' beliefs?
o: Their belief may not match the research results
Their belief is proved completely right
qs.why: 많은 학생이 음악이 도움이 된다고 믿지만 연구는 다른 모습을 보여 줘요.

items.title: Click, Try, Return
items.text: Online shopping has changed how we buy almost everything. Shoppers can compare prices in seconds, read reviews from other customers, and have items delivered to their door. (A), they cannot touch, try on, or test the products before paying. (B), many returns are caused by clothes that look different on the screen than in real life. Stores have responded by offering free returns, so shoppers feel safer ordering items they are unsure about.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 장점 뒤에 단점이 오므로 However, 단점의 구체적 예는 For example이에요.

qs.q: What can shoppers NOT do when buying online?
o: Try on or test the products before paying
qs.why: 온라인에서는 구입 전에 만지거나 입어 볼 수 없어요.

qs.q: What does "so" in the last sentence show?
o: A contrast between stores and customers
A result: free returns make shoppers feel safer
An example of an unsafe product
qs.why: so는 결과를 나타내요: 무료 반품 덕분에 더 안심하고 주문해요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Online shopping is convenient but has some drawbacks
Stores should stop selling clothes online
qs.why: 온라인 쇼핑의 편리함과 단점을 함께 다뤄요.

items.title: The Camel's Hump
items.text: Camels are well adapted to life in the desert. Their wide, flat feet spread out on the sand, which stops them from sinking. A camel can also go for days without drinking. (A), it does not store water in its hump, as many people believe. (B), the hump holds fat, which the animal can break down for energy when food is hard to find. In other words, the hump works like a food supply rather than a water tank.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 혹에 물이 없다는 반전은 However, 대신 지방이 있다는 것은 Instead예요.

qs.q: What does the hump of a camel store?
qs.why: 혹에는 지방이 저장되어 있어요.

qs.q: What does the last sentence do?
o: It adds a new and unrelated fact
It restates the idea with a simple comparison
It describes the cause of a problem
qs.why: In other words는 앞 내용을 쉬운 비유로 다시 말해요.

qs.q: Why are a camel's feet wide and flat?
o: They stop the camel from sinking into the sand
They help the camel store water
They keep the camel's body cool
They help the camel find food
qs.why: 넓고 평평한 발은 모래에 빠지지 않게 해요.

items.title: Slow Progress on the Guitar
items.text: I started learning the guitar six months ago, and my progress has been slower than I hoped. Although I practice for thirty minutes every day, my fingers still hurt, and some chords sound terrible. My teacher says this is normal and tells me not to feel discouraged. (A) giving up, she suggests that I record myself once a week. When I listen to old recordings, I can hear how much I have improved. That small habit has changed my attitude, and I now look forward to practice rather than dreading it.

qs.q: Which expression best fills (A)?
qs.why: 포기하는 대신 녹음을 해 보라는 뜻이므로 Instead of가 알맞아요. 뒤에 동명사(giving up)가 와요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why the guitar is the hardest instrument
How to choose a good guitar teacher
How a simple habit helped the writer stay positive about learning
The writer's plan to give up music
qs.why: 녹음하는 작은 습관이 학습 태도를 바꿨다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What does the teacher suggest?
o: Practicing for two hours a day
Recording a practice session once a week
qs.why: 일주일에 한 번 녹음해 보라고 했어요.

qs.q: How has the writer's attitude changed?
o: From dreading practice to looking forward to it
From loving practice to avoiding it
From teaching others to learning alone
From using a guitar to using a piano
qs.why: 연습이 두렵던 상태에서 기대하는 상태로 바뀌었어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "discouraged" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: discouraged는 낙담한, 의욕을 잃은이라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: More Than Books
items.text: Public libraries are no longer just places to borrow books. Many now lend tools, musical instruments, and even board games. (A), they run free classes in coding, cooking, and languages. (B) these services, a library card can be worth hundreds of dollars a year. Some people believe that the Internet makes libraries unnecessary. (C), librarians point out that millions of people still lack a fast connection or a quiet place to study at home.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 대여 서비스에 수업을 덧붙이는 In addition, 서비스 덕분에는 Thanks to예요.

qs.q: Which word best fills (C)?
qs.why: 도서관이 불필요하다는 믿음과 반대되는 사실을 말하므로 However예요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Modern libraries offer many services beyond books
Free classes are a waste of money
The Internet has closed most libraries
qs.why: 현대 도서관이 책 외에도 다양한 서비스를 제공한다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What do librarians say about the Internet?
o: It is too slow for libraries to use
It should be banned in public libraries
It is cheaper than a library card
Many people still lack a fast connection or quiet place at home
qs.why: 수백만 명이 여전히 빠른 연결이나 조용한 공간이 없다고 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about libraries?
o: They still serve people who lack resources at home
qs.why: 집에 자원이 없는 사람들에게 여전히 필요하다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Electric Cars: Promise and Problems
items.text: Electric cars produce no exhaust, so they keep city air cleaner. Their running costs are also low, since electricity is usually cheaper than gasoline. (A), buyers face some real problems. A new electric car often costs more than a similar gasoline model, and charging stations are still rare in rural areas. (B), governments in many countries offer money to help people buy one. Experts expect that as batteries become cheaper, these obstacles will gradually disappear.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 장점 뒤에 문제를 말하므로 However, 문제 때문에 지원금이 있으므로 For this reason이에요.

qs.q: Why are the running costs of electric cars low?
o: Electricity is usually cheaper than gasoline
They are much smaller than other cars
qs.why: 전기가 보통 휘발유보다 싸기 때문이에요.

qs.q: In the last sentence, "these obstacles" refers to
o: cheap electricity and low running costs
high prices and a lack of charging stations
qs.why: these obstacles는 앞에서 말한 높은 가격과 부족한 충전소를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What do experts expect?
o: Cheaper batteries will make the problems smaller
qs.why: 배터리가 싸지면 장애물이 점차 사라질 것이라고 해요.

items.title: The Science of Kimchi
items.text: Kimchi has been part of Korean meals for centuries. [1] Its flavor comes from fermentation. [2] When vegetables are salted and stored, harmless bacteria begin to grow and produce lactic acid. [3] The acid gives kimchi its sour taste and also protects it from spoiling. [4] Today, scientists study these bacteria because they may be good for the stomach.

qs.q:
Where would the following sentence best fit?
"That is why it can be kept for months in a cool place."
qs.why: That is why 앞에는 보존이 가능한 이유(산이 부패를 막음)가 와야 하므로 [4]가 알맞아요.

qs.q: Which word could replace "because" in the last sentence without changing the meaning?
qs.why: because는 이유를 나타내며 since로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why Koreans eat kimchi at every meal
How to salt vegetables at home
Which bacteria are harmful to the stomach
How fermentation gives kimchi its taste and helps it last
qs.why: 발효가 김치의 맛과 보존에 미치는 영향을 설명해요.

qs.q: What does lactic acid do to kimchi?
o: It makes it sweeter and softer
It makes it sour and protects it from spoiling
It stops the bacteria from growing
qs.why: 산은 신맛을 내고 부패를 막아 줘요.

items.title: A Letter of Inquiry
items.text:
Dear Ms. Alvarez,

I am a first-year high school student, and I am writing to ask about volunteer opportunities at your science museum. I have been interested in astronomy since I joined my school's science club. (A), I am free on Saturday mornings and during the summer holidays. (B), I understand that most volunteers must be at least sixteen, and I will turn sixteen in November. (C), I would be grateful if you could let me know whether I may apply now or should wait.

Yours sincerely,
Hyun-woo Seo

qs.q: Which set best fills (A), (B), and (C)?
qs.why: 시간 여유를 덧붙이는 Moreover, 나이 제한이라는 걸림돌을 말하는 However, 그래서 문의하는 Therefore예요.

qs.q: Why did Hyun-woo write this letter?
o: To ask whether he can volunteer at the museum
To apply for a paid job as a guide
To complain about a museum exhibit
To invite the museum to his school
qs.why: 박물관 봉사 기회에 대해 문의하는 편지예요.

qs.q: When is Hyun-woo free to volunteer?
o: On Saturday mornings and during summer holidays
qs.why: 토요일 오전과 여름방학에 시간이 된다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does he mention November?
o: He will reach the minimum age then
The summer holidays will end then
qs.why: 11월에 16세가 되어 최소 연령 조건을 충족해요.

qs.q: What is the tone of the letter?
qs.why: 정중하고 격식 있는 어조예요.

items.title: Why Noon Is Not the Same Everywhere
items.text: Imagine calling a friend overseas at noon your time, only to wake her at midnight. This happens because the Earth is divided into 24 time zones. As the Earth turns, the sun reaches different places at different moments, (A) noon in Seoul comes many hours before noon in London. Before the 1800s, every town set its own clock by the sun. (B), the invention of railways made this system confusing, since a train passenger had to adjust a watch at every station. Countries therefore agreed to share standard time zones.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 해가 다른 시각에 도달한 결과가 so, 옛 방식이 철도 때문에 문제가 된 대조가 However예요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to make a clock that uses the sun
Why Seoul is ahead of every other city
How railways were built in the 1800s
Why time zones exist and how they came to be shared
qs.why: 시간대가 생긴 이유와 표준 시간대가 정해진 과정을 설명해요.

qs.q: Why was the old system confusing for train passengers?
o: They had to adjust their watch at every station
qs.why: 역마다 시계를 맞춰야 했기 때문이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "standard" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: standard time은 모두에게 같은 표준 시간을 뜻해요.

items.title: Two Street Food Cultures
items.text: Street food markets in Southeast Asia and in Korea may look alike at first glance. Both offer cheap, freshly made dishes cooked in front of the customer, and both attract crowds in the evening. (A), the experience differs in several ways. In Bangkok, many vendors sell dishes with strong spices and fresh herbs. (B), in Seoul's traditional markets, the most popular items are often fried or grilled snacks eaten while standing. Despite these differences, both kinds of markets show how food can bring a community together.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 닮은 점을 말한 뒤 차이를 말하므로 However, 두 도시의 대비는 By contrast예요.

qs.q: What does the second sentence do?
o: It explains why the markets are different
It gives an example of a Bangkok dish
It tells what happens in the morning
It describes ways the two kinds of markets are similar
qs.why: Both ... and both ... 로 공통점을 설명해요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Bangkok has better street food than Seoul
Street food is unhealthy for communities
Street food markets in two regions are alike in some ways and different in others
Markets in Korea only sell fried snacks
qs.why: 두 시장의 공통점과 차이점을 비교하는 글이에요.

qs.q: What does "Despite these differences" suggest about the writer's view?
o: The differences are too big to compare
The markets share an important common value
One market should copy the other
qs.why: 차이에도 불구하고 공동체를 모은다는 공통점을 강조해요.

items.title: Junk in Orbit
items.text: Since the first satellite was launched in 1957, thousands of objects have been sent into orbit. Most were meant to be temporary. (A), when satellites stop working, many stay in space as junk. Today more than 30,000 pieces larger than a tennis ball are tracked, and millions of smaller pieces cannot be tracked at all. Moving at about 28,000 kilometers per hour, even a tiny fragment can damage a spacecraft. (B), space agencies now plan satellites that can be pulled out of orbit once their work is done.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 임시용이었지만 실제로는 남는다는 대조(However), 위험의 결과로 계획을 세우는 As a result예요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to track objects larger than a tennis ball
Why spacecraft travel at high speed
The growing problem of junk in space and efforts to deal with it
qs.why: 우주 쓰레기 문제와 대응 노력을 다뤄요.

qs.q: Why can a tiny fragment damage a spacecraft?
o: It is made of heavy metal
It moves at an extremely high speed
It is hotter than the sun
qs.why: 시속 약 28,000km로 움직이기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What are space agencies planning?
o: A ban on all satellite launches
Satellites that can be removed from orbit after use
Larger satellites that stay for longer
A way to track the smallest pieces
qs.why: 임무 후 궤도에서 제거할 수 있는 위성을 계획해요.

items.title: What Makes a Good Friend?
items.text: What makes a good friend? Some people say it is someone who shares your interests. Others say it is someone who is always available. (A), I believe that the most important quality is honesty. A friend who tells you the truth kindly, even when it is uncomfortable, helps you to grow. (B), a friend who only says what you want to hear may be pleasant, but cannot be fully trusted. (C), true friendship depends less on fun times than on trust.

qs.q: Which set best fills (A), (B), and (C)?
qs.why: 다른 견해와 대비되는 However, 정직한 친구와 대비되는 In contrast, 결론의 In short예요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the first three sentences?
o: To list the writer's favorite friends
To prove that honesty is unimportant
To present other views before stating the writer's own
qs.why: 다른 사람들의 의견을 먼저 제시한 뒤 자신의 의견을 말해요.

qs.q: According to the writer, what is the most important quality of a friend?
qs.why: 필자는 정직을 가장 중요하게 봐요.

qs.q: What does the writer say about a friend who only says what you want to hear?
o: Such a friend is the best kind of friend
Such a friend is pleasant but not fully trustworthy
Such a friend always tells the truth
Such a friend is difficult to find
qs.why: 듣기 좋은 말만 하면 즐겁지만 완전히 믿을 수는 없다고 했어요.

items.title: Visitor Information
items.text:
VISITOR INFORMATION: Maple Science Museum

The museum is open from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Tuesday through Sunday. Admission is free for children under seven. In addition, students aged seven to eighteen pay half price if they show a valid school ID. Please note that the Space Hall will be closed for repairs until June 30. (A), the Ocean Gallery on the second floor is open as usual, and its new whale exhibit has been very popular. Photographs are welcome, (B) flash photography is not allowed near the display of old documents.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 닫힌 전시관과 대비되는 열린 전시관은 On the other hand, 허용과 제한을 잇는 접속어는 but이에요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of this notice?
o: To advertise a new job at the museum
To announce that the museum is closing forever
To ask visitors to donate old documents
To give visitors useful information about the museum
qs.why: 방문객에게 박물관 이용 정보를 알려 줘요.

qs.q: Who pays half price?
o: Students aged seven to eighteen with a school ID
qs.why: 7~18세 학생은 학생증이 있으면 반값이에요.

qs.q: Which statement is true?
o: The museum is open every day of the week
The Space Hall will reopen after June 30
The Ocean Gallery is on the first floor
qs.why: 우주관은 6월 30일까지 수리로 닫혀요. 박물관은 화~일 개방, 해양관은 2층이에요.

items.title: Training for a Marathon
items.text: Training for a marathon takes months of careful planning. In the beginning, most coaches advise runners to build their weekly distance slowly. (A), a beginner who suddenly runs twenty kilometers is likely to be injured. After about two months, runners usually add a long run on weekends. Gradually the distance grows from ten kilometers to thirty. (B), the final weeks are different: runners cut their distance and rest so that their legs are fresh on race day. Many first-time runners are surprised that doing less can make them faster.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 천천히 늘리지 않으면(Otherwise) 부상, 거리를 늘리는 단계와 대비되는 마지막 주(However)예요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why marathons are held in the morning
How runners should plan their training for a marathon
qs.why: 마라톤 준비 훈련 계획을 설명하는 글이에요.

qs.q: What do runners do in the final weeks?
o: They run thirty kilometers every day
They stop all exercise for a month
They add a second long run
qs.why: 마지막 몇 주에는 거리를 줄이고 쉬어요.

qs.q: Which step comes right after building weekly distance slowly?
o: Adding a long run on weekends
qs.why: 약 두 달 뒤 주말 장거리 달리기를 추가해요.

items.title: Saving Water
items.text: Water seems unlimited when it flows from the tap, yet fresh water is scarce. Only about three percent of the world's water is fresh, and most of that is frozen. Households can reduce their use in simple ways. (A), turning off the tap while brushing your teeth saves around six liters a minute. (B), fixing a leaking faucet can save thousands of liters a year. Farms and factories use far more water than homes do, so individual effort alone is not enough. Governments and companies must also change how they use water.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 간단한 방법의 예(For example)와 또 다른 비슷한 방법(Similarly)이에요.

qs.q: What does "so" in the second-to-last sentence show?
o: A contrast with the idea of saving water
An example of a household habit
A result of farms and factories using more water
qs.why: 농장과 공장이 더 많이 쓰므로 개인의 노력만으로는 부족하다는 결과예요.

qs.q: What is the writer's conclusion?
o: Households alone can solve the problem
Both individuals and large water users need to act
Fresh water will never run out
qs.why: 개인뿐 아니라 정부와 기업도 변해야 한다고 결론지어요.

qs.q: About how much of the world's water is fresh?
qs.why: 세계 물의 약 3퍼센트만 담수예요.

items.title: A New Way to Read
items.text: Until the 1800s, blind people could read only with books printed in large raised letters. These books were huge, expensive, and slow to read, so very few were available. A young blind student found a better way. He used patterns of six dots, which fingertips can recognize much faster than letter shapes. (A), a page could be read quickly and written with a simple tool. (B), the system spread worldwide and is still used today.

qs.q: Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?
qs.why: 점자의 효과를 결과로 이어 주는 As a result, 시간이 지나 퍼졌다는 Eventually예요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why large books were popular in schools
How to write with a simple tool
Why blind students prefer listening to reading
How a new system of dots made reading easier for blind people
qs.why: 점자가 시각장애인의 읽기를 쉽게 만든 과정을 다뤄요.

qs.q: Why were the old books hard to use?
o: They were printed in many languages
They were huge, expensive, and slow to read
qs.why: 크고 비싸며 읽는 속도가 느렸어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "recognize" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: recognize는 알아보다, 식별하다라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Robots on the Hospital Floor
items.text: Hospitals around the world are beginning to use robots. Some carry medicine and meals through long corridors, while others help surgeons perform delicate operations with great accuracy. Supporters say that robots reduce mistakes and give nurses more time with patients. Nevertheless, there are concerns. A machine cannot comfort a frightened child, and it costs millions of dollars to buy and maintain. For these reasons, most experts believe that robots should assist medical staff, not replace them.

qs.q: What does "Nevertheless" signal?
o: A contrast with the benefits just mentioned
A result of the robots' accuracy
A time order of two events
qs.why: Nevertheless는 앞의 장점과 대비되는 우려를 이끌어요.

qs.q: What is the function of the sentence "A machine cannot comfort a frightened child"?
o: It explains how robots carry medicine
It shows that nurses dislike robots
It repeats the benefits for patients
It gives an example of a limit of robots
qs.why: 로봇의 한계를 보여 주는 예시 문장이에요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Robots are useful in hospitals but should support, not replace, staff
qs.why: 로봇은 도움이 되지만 의료진을 대체해서는 안 된다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: Which is mentioned as a benefit of robots?
o: They cost less than human staff
They reduce mistakes and give nurses more time with patients
qs.why: 실수를 줄이고 간호사가 환자와 보낼 시간을 늘려 줘요.

items.title: Planning the Class Trip
items.text:
Mina: Have you decided where we should go for the class trip?
Joon: I like the science museum. It has a new space exhibition.
Mina: That sounds interesting. However, it's quite far from school, and the bus ride takes two hours.
Joon: True. On the other hand, the aquarium is only forty minutes away.
Mina: Besides, tickets for the aquarium are cheaper.
Joon: Then let's suggest the aquarium. We can visit the museum on our own later.
Mina: Good idea. I'll write the proposal tonight, and you can add the price list.
Joon: Deal.

qs.q: What does Mina's "However" show?
o: She sees a problem with Joon's suggestion
She gives an example of an exhibition
qs.why: However 뒤에서 박물관이 멀다는 문제점을 말해요.

qs.q: What does "Besides" introduce?
o: A reason to choose the museum
A result of the long bus ride
An additional reason in favor of the aquarium
qs.why: Besides는 수족관을 선택하는 또 하나의 이유(싼 입장권)를 덧붙여요.

qs.q: What do they decide to do?
o: Propose the aquarium for the class trip
qs.why: 수족관을 제안하기로 해요.

qs.q: What will Joon do for the proposal?
qs.why: Mina가 제안서를 쓰고 Joon이 가격표를 추가해요.

items.title: Sharing the Poster Work
items.text:
Sora: We only have three days left for the poster. Who is doing what?
Ethan: I'll draw the charts. After that, I can help with the layout.
Sora: Great. Meanwhile, I'll write the text, and Dahye will collect the photos.
Dahye: Actually, I haven't started yet. I was sick on Monday.
Sora: Oh, I'm sorry. In that case, I'll collect the photos myself. You can proofread everything at the end.
Dahye: That works. Otherwise, I'd be too stressed. Thanks!
Ethan: So we're set. Let's meet again on Thursday and check our progress.

qs.q: What does "Meanwhile" show about Sora's plan?
o: She will write the text while Ethan draws the charts
She will write the text after the photos are done
She will not write any text
She will draw the charts instead of Ethan
qs.why: Meanwhile은 같은 시간에 다른 일을 한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does Sora change the plan for the photos?
o: Dahye does not want to join the group
Dahye was sick and has not started
qs.why: Dahye가 아파서 시작하지 못했기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does Dahye mean by "Otherwise, I'd be too stressed"?
o: If Sora said thank you, she would be stressed
If the poster were finished, she would be stressed
If she had to collect the photos herself, she would be too stressed
If Ethan helped her, she would be stressed
qs.why: Otherwise는 '그렇지 않으면', 즉 사진까지 모아야 했다면 부담이 컸을 것이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What will Dahye do for the poster?
qs.why: 마지막에 전체를 교정하기로 해요.

items.title: At the Restaurant
items.text:
Waiter: Welcome. Are you ready to order?
Customer: Yes. I'd like the grilled salmon, please.
Waiter: I'm afraid the salmon is sold out. Instead, I can recommend the roast chicken.
Customer: Hmm. I'm allergic to nuts. Does the chicken come with a nut sauce?
Waiter: Actually, yes, it does. Still, we can serve it with plain gravy.
Customer: In that case, I'll have it with the gravy. And a side salad, too.
Waiter: Certainly. Would you like anything to drink as well?
Customer: Just water, thanks.

qs.q: What does "Instead" show?
o: The waiter offers a substitute for the sold-out dish
The waiter refuses to serve the customer
The waiter repeats the customer's order
qs.why: Instead는 품절된 메뉴 대신 다른 메뉴를 제안해요.

qs.q: Why does the customer ask about the sauce?
o: The customer wants a cheaper dish
The customer is in a hurry
The customer is allergic to nuts
qs.why: 견과류 알레르기가 있기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does "Still" show in the waiter's answer?
o: He agrees that the chicken is unsafe
He asks the customer to leave
He offers a solution despite the problem
qs.why: 문제가 있어도 해결책(plain gravy)을 제시해요.

qs.q: What will the customer order?
o: Grilled salmon with a side salad and water
Roast chicken with plain gravy, a side salad, and water
Roast chicken with nut sauce and water
qs.why: 일반 그레이비를 곁들인 로스트 치킨, 샐러드, 물을 주문해요.

items.title: A New Date for the Cleanup
items.text:
Hana: Our park cleanup was canceled because of the rain.
Min: That's disappointing. We need a new date, then.
Hana: What about this Saturday? The forecast looks sunny.
Min: Unfortunately, I have a dentist appointment in the morning. But I'm free after lunch.
Hana: Fine. Moreover, more members can join in the afternoon since soccer practice ends at noon.
Min: That's true. As a result, we can clean a bigger area.
Hana: Exactly. I'll text everyone tonight.

qs.q: Why was the cleanup canceled?
qs.why: 비 때문에 취소되었어요.

qs.q: Why does Min prefer the afternoon?
o: The forecast is bad in the morning
He has a dentist appointment in the morning
qs.why: 오전에 치과 예약이 있기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does "Moreover" introduce?
o: A reason to cancel the cleanup again
Another reason for choosing the afternoon
qs.why: Moreover는 오후가 좋은 또 하나의 이유(더 많은 회원 참여)를 덧붙여요.

qs.q: According to Min, what will happen if more members join?
o: They can clean a bigger area
They will need a new park
qs.why: As a result 뒤에서 더 넓은 구역을 청소할 수 있다고 해요.

items.title: Was the Movie Too Long?
items.text:
Jun: I thought the movie was too long. Nearly three hours!
Yuna: I see your point. Still, the story needed that time to develop the characters.
Jun: Maybe. But the middle part dragged on. For instance, the scene in the train station lasted twenty minutes.
Yuna: Okay, that scene was slow. Nevertheless, the ending made it worthwhile for me.
Jun: Honestly, the music was the best part. It was beautiful, so I could forgive the length.
Yuna: See? We agree on something after all!

qs.q: What example does Jun give of the middle part dragging on?
o: A twenty-minute scene in a train station
The final scene of the movie
A scene with too many characters
qs.why: For instance 뒤에 기차역 장면이 20분 이어졌다는 예가 나와요.

qs.q: What does Yuna's "Still" show?
o: She changes the topic to music
She says she did not see the movie
She partly agrees but defends the movie's length
qs.why: Still은 인정하면서도 반대 의견을 이어 줘요.

qs.q: What does "so" show in Jun's last turn?
o: A contrast between music and story
An example of a long scene
A result: the music made him forgive the length
qs.why: 아름다운 음악 때문에 길이를 용서할 수 있었다는 결과예요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the two speakers?
o: They both hated the whole movie
They disagree on some points but share an opinion about the music
They have not decided what to watch
qs.why: 영화 길이에는 이견이 있지만 음악에는 의견이 같아요.

items.title: A Better Study Plan
items.text:
Teacher: You wanted to talk about your study plan?
Student: Yes. I study from 7 to 11 every night, but my grades are not improving.
Teacher: How about your sleep?
Student: I usually sleep five hours. In addition, I skip breakfast.
Teacher: I see. That may be the problem. Although you study a lot, your brain is tired.
Student: So you think I should study less?
Teacher: Not exactly. Rather, you should study smarter. For example, take a ten-minute break every hour and go to bed by eleven.
Student: I'll try that. Thank you!

qs.q: What problem does the student describe?
o: Long study hours are not improving the grades
The student has no time to study
qs.why: 오래 공부해도 성적이 오르지 않는다고 말해요.

qs.q: What does "In addition" add?
o: A reason the student studies late
An example of a good habit
A result of sleeping five hours
Skipping breakfast as another poor habit
qs.why: In addition은 수면 부족에 더해 아침을 거르는 습관을 덧붙여요.

qs.q: What does the teacher mean by "Rather, you should study smarter"?
o: Study more effectively instead of simply studying less
qs.why: Rather는 '오히려'로, 덜 하는 게 아니라 더 효과적으로 하라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "For example" introduce?
o: Reasons for the student's low grades
A list of the student's subjects
qs.why: For example 뒤에 휴식과 취침 시간 같은 구체적 방법이 나와요.

qs.q: What does the teacher think is causing the problem?
o: A tired brain from too little rest
A lack of interest in the subject
qs.why: 공부를 많이 해도 뇌가 피곤하다고 말해요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
He studied hard; ______, he failed the test.
items.why: 열심히 공부했지만 떨어졌으므로 대조의 however예요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
The room was small. ______, it was clean and bright.
items.why: 작지만 깨끗하고 밝았다는 양보/대조 관계이므로 Nevertheless예요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
Many animals sleep through the winter. ______, bears stay in their dens for months.
items.why: 곰은 겨울잠을 자는 동물의 예이므로 For example이에요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
She speaks Korean and English. ______, she is learning Spanish.
items.why: 이미 하는 언어에 더해 스페인어도 배우므로 In addition이에요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
First, mix the flour and eggs. ______, pour the mixture into a pan.
items.why: 조리 순서의 다음 단계이므로 Next예요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression.
______ the heavy rain, the game continued.
items.why: 명사구 앞에서 양보를 나타내는 것은 Despite예요. Although와 Because는 절을 이끌고, However는 문장 앞 접속부사예요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
You should leave now. ______, you will miss the train.
items.why: 서두르지 않으면 기차를 놓친다는 뜻이므로 Otherwise예요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
Some students prefer online classes. ______, others like learning in person.
items.why: 두 가지 선호를 대비하므로 On the other hand예요.

items.q:
What does "In fact" mainly do in this text?
Ana seems shy. In fact, she hardly speaks in class.
o: It gives a stronger, more specific statement
items.why: In fact는 앞 내용을 더 강하고 구체적으로 보충해요.

items.q:
Which order of the sentences is best?
(a) Finally, serve it with rice.
(b) First, cut the vegetables.
(c) Then fry them for five minutes.
items.why: First, Then, Finally의 순서 표지어에 따라 (b)-(c)-(a)예요.

items.q:
Which sentence should come right after the following?
"Plastic takes hundreds of years to break down."
o: In contrast, it breaks down within a few weeks.
Otherwise, many countries have banned plastic bags.
Similarly, glass bottles are made from sand.
Therefore, reducing its use helps the environment.
items.why: 문제점(분해가 오래 걸림) 뒤에 결과/결론을 이어 주는 것이 자연스러워요.

items.q:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
(1) Regular exercise keeps the heart strong. (2) It also helps people sleep better at night. (3) My uncle bought a new red car last week. (4) Even a short walk every day can improve your mood.
items.why: (3)만 운동의 장점이라는 주제와 관련이 없어요.

items.q:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
(1) The Han River is a popular place for leisure in Seoul. (2) Many families have picnics along its banks. (3) Many cyclists ride along the paths beside the water. (4) Calculators were first sold in the 1960s.
items.why: (4)는 한강 이야기와 무관해서 흐름을 끊어요.

items.q:
Where does the sentence best fit?
"Another reason is that they use their phones in bed."
Many students find it hard to wake up early. (1) One reason is that they go to bed too late. (2) The light from the screens makes it harder for the brain to relax. (3) Experts therefore advise turning off screens an hour before sleep. (4)
items.why: Another reason은 One reason 바로 뒤에 와야 하고, 다음 문장의 the screens가 휴대전화를 가리키므로 (2)예요.

items.q:
Where does the sentence best fit?
"However, not all of them are harmful."
Bacteria are often thought of as germs that cause disease. (1) Some live in our stomachs and help us digest food. (2) Others are used to make yogurt and cheese. (3) Scientists keep discovering new types every year. (4)
items.why: However로 앞의 '세균=해롭다'는 통념과 대비되므로 첫 문장 바로 뒤 (1)이에요.

items.q: Which connective best begins the final paragraph of an essay?
items.why: To sum up은 마지막에 요약·결론을 이끌어요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
Dad cooked dinner. ______, I set the table.
items.why: 두 일이 동시에 일어나므로 Meanwhile이에요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
I did not go to the party. ______, I stayed home and read a book.
items.why: 가지 않고 그 대신 집에 있었으므로 Instead예요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
Cats groom themselves often. ______, birds spend time cleaning their feathers.
items.why: 비슷한 행동을 덧붙이므로 Similarly예요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression.
Fruits ______ apples and pears are rich in fiber.
items.why: such as는 예를 들 때 써요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression.
The flight was cancelled ______ a storm.
items.why: 뒤에 명사구(a storm)가 오므로 due to예요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression.
______ your help, we finished early.
items.why: 도움 덕분에 일찍 끝났다는 뜻이므로 Thanks to예요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression.
______ being tired, she kept running.
items.why: 피곤했지만 계속 달렸으므로 양보의 In spite of예요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
It was very cold. ______, we went swimming in the sea.
items.why: 문장 앞에서 쓰는 접속부사는 Even so예요. Even though는 절을 이끄는 접속사예요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression.
I will call you ______ I arrive.
items.why: 도착하자마자 전화하겠다는 뜻이므로 as soon as예요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression.
Take an umbrella ______ it rains.
items.why: 비가 올 경우를 대비해서라는 뜻이므로 in case예요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression.
You may borrow the book ______ you return it on Friday.
items.why: 금요일에 반납한다는 조건이면 빌릴 수 있으므로 as long as예요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
I enjoy outdoor sports. ______, I love hiking.
items.why: 야외 스포츠 중 특히 하이킹이므로 In particular예요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
The factory closed. ______, hundreds of workers lost their jobs.
items.why: 공장이 문을 닫은 결과이므로 Consequently예요.

items.q:
Choose the best connective.
The film was a flop. ______, almost nobody liked it.
items.why: 앞 표현을 쉬운 말로 바꿔 말하므로 In other words예요.

items.good: Although it rained, we went hiking.
bad: Although it rained, but we went hiking.
Despite it rained, we went hiking.
Although of the rain, we went hiking.
items.rule: Although는 절을 이끄는 양보 접속사이고, 뒤 절에 but을 함께 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: Because of the storm, the match was cancelled.
bad: Because the storm, the match was cancelled.
Because of the storm was strong, the match was cancelled.
Because of the storm, the match cancelled.

cz.st: ___ the storm, the match was cancelled.
